question: How is the compensation for a hallmarked item that is impure calculated?

question: According to the S.O. 205(E) notification, on what date did the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, 2020, come into force, and what specific documentary evidence must an applicant provide regarding their Quality Control (QC) personnel as per the BIS application checklist?
answer:
The Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, 2020, published under notification number S.O. 205(E), came into force with effect from the 15th day of January, 2021 [1][2].

question: I manage a small manufacturing unit and have noticed that the BIS factory inspection agent assigned to us is a former supplier from our own industry. The agent has not disclosed this prior association. According to the guidelines for factory surveillance, what specific professional obligation has the agent failed to meet, and what is the expected course of action regarding such associations?
answer:
The agent has failed to meet the professional obligation of impartiality under the code of ethics by not disclosing their past and present association with the entity being assessed [1].

Regarding the expected course of action, any instance noticed that casts doubt on the ethics and integrity of the agent shall be reported and submitted by the Head of the Branch Office (BO) to the Deputy Director General (DDG) of Certification through DDGR for further appropriate action [2].

**Sources:**
[1] Guidelines for Factory Surveillance (25 Feb 2026): Annexure-II, p. 18, dated 2026-02-25 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/FactorySurveillance-Guidelines-25Feb2026.pdf#page=18

question: Can the Bureau of Indian Standards adopt standards created by other organizations as Indian Standards?
answer:
Yes, the Bureau may adopt as an Indian Standard any standard established by any other institution in India or outside India in relation to any goods, article, process, system, or service [1][2]. This adoption can include necessary modifications in accordance with the prescribed procedure [2].

question: I own a small business registered on the Udyam Portal with plant and machinery investment under ₹1 crore and the previous year's turnover below ₹5 crore, certified by a Chartered Accountant. Do I need to comply with the 2024 Quality Control Order for insulated flasks, bottles, and containers for domestic use?
answer:
No, you do not need to comply with the 2024 Quality Control Order for insulated flasks, bottles, and containers for domestic use [1].

The Quality Control Order does not apply to goods or articles manufactured by an enterprise registered on the Udyam Portal where the original investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed one crore rupees and the previous financial year's turnover does not exceed five crore rupees, as certified by a Chartered Accountant [1].

question: I am a manufacturer of components that are meant to be integrated into larger host products. I have implemented e-labelling for my products. question: I own a manufacturing unit that has recently been issued a Certificate of Conformity. If my certification is currently suspended or has expired, can I still use the certificate to certify that my products meet the required standards? Additionally, what are my obligations regarding the labeling of these products and maintaining documentation?
answer:
No, you cannot use the certificate of conformity during deferment or suspension, or after the expiry or cancellation of the certificate [1].

Regarding your obligations:
1. You must comply with the provisions of the conformity assessment scheme under which the certificate of conformity is granted, including all labelling and marking requirements [1].
2. You must maintain records as specified by the Bureau from time to time [1].

**Sources:**

question: Which specific legal instrument amended the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, 2020 to insert a clause regarding its application, and which four distinct categories of goods are listed under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (Scheme II) for self-declaration of conformity?
answer:
The legal instrument that amended the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts Order, 2020 to insert a clause regarding its application is the Hallmarking of Gold Jewellery and Gold Artefacts (Second Amendment) Order, 2021 [1].

The four distinct categories of goods listed under the Compulsory Registration Scheme (Scheme II) for self-declaration of conformity are: [2]
1. Electronics and IT Goods notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology [2].
2. Solar Photovoltaics, Systems, Devices and Components notified by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy [2].
3. Chemicals notified by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers [2].
4. Textile material notified by the Ministry of Textiles [2].

**Sources:**
[1] Hallmarking Order, June 2021: p. 1, dated 2021-06-23 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/qc-order-June-2021-2.pdf#page=1
[2] Scheme II (CRS registration) page: Scheme - II (Registration Scheme) | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/scheme-ii-registration-scheme/?lang=en

question: My factory needs to re-test only the failed parameters of a previous sample. If I choose to test the remnants of the original sample, can I skip checking other parameters, and what are the witness requirements and costs for this process?
answer:
Testing of other parameters may be foregone by the Branch Office (BO), if felt technically appropriate [1].

For witnessing the test, a separate charge of rupees ten thousand per day, along with the cost of travel, boarding, and lodging for the BIS official, shall be payable by the manufacturer [1]. Additionally, the concerned officer-in-charge and the Quality Assurance (QA) officer must personally remain present and witness such testing either in a BIS laboratory or a BIS-recognised/empanelled laboratory [1].

**Sources:**
[1] Guidelines for Sample Coding and Retesting of Samples: p. 1, dated 2025-07-14 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/07/Guidelines-Samples-Coding-Retesting.pdf#page=1

question: What specific declaration must a firm’s representative sign in Form IX regarding their manufacturing equipment, and how can a consumer verify the authenticity of a hallmarked article through a BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre?
answer:
In Form IX, the firm’s representative declares that the listed machinery details are available with them, that they have verified the availability of the machinery during their inspection, and that they will send prior intimation to the Bureau whenever any machinery is not available [1].

A consumer can get their jewellery or sample tested from any BIS Recognized Assaying & Hallmarking Centre, which undertakes testing on priority on a chargeable basis and issues an Assay Report with proper identifications marked on the article [2]. Additionally, consumers can verify the authenticity of the jewellery or artefact by using the 'Verify HUID feature' on the BIS CARE App [3].

**Sources:**
[1] BIS (Hallmarking) Regulations, 2018 (incl. Amdt 1): Form-IX, p. 86, dated 2018 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/BIS-Hallmarking-Regulations-2018-Incorp.-Amdt-1.pdf#page=86
[2] Hallmarking overview: Hallmarking overview | https://www.bis.gov.in/hallmarking-overview/?lang=en
[3] Guidelines for Jewellers (Jul 2026): p. 1, dated 2026-07-02 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Guidelines-for-Jewellers.pdf#page=1

question: What are the specific hallmarking fees payable by a jeweller to an Assaying and Hallmarking Centre for a silver article, including the minimum consignment charge, and what is the mandatory cooling period before a jeweller can reapply for registration if their previous registration was cancelled under Regulation 7(1) of the BIS (Hallmarking) Regulations, 2018?
answer:
The hallmarking fees payable by a jeweller to a recognised Assaying and Hallmarking Centre for a silver article are Rs. 35/- per article, with a minimum fee for a consignment of Rs. 150/-, and applicable taxes as per prevalent rates levied in addition [1].

The mandatory cooling period before the Bureau will accept an application for the grant of a certificate of registration, in cases of cancellation or non-renewal due to reasons given in clause (e) of sub-regulation (1) of Regulation 7, is one year from the date of passing [2].

**Sources:**
[1] Hallmarking Amendment Regulations, 2026: Regulation 2., p. 3, dated 2026-09-14 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Gazette-Notification-of-Hallmarking-Published.pdf#page=3

question: What are the specific technical criteria for equipment to be exempted from the Electronics and Information Technology Goods Order under S.O. 1246(E)?
answer:
Highly Specialized Equipment (HSE) is exempted from the Order provided it is manufactured or imported in less than 100 units per model per year and satisfies any of the following technical criteria [1]:

* Equipment powered by a three-phase power supply [1].
* Equipment powered by a single-phase power supply with a current rating exceeding 16 Amperes [1].
* Equipment with dimensions exceeding 1.5 m x 0.8 m [1].
* Equipment with a weight exceeding 80 Kg [1].

**Sources:**
[1] Electronics & IT Goods (Requirement of Compulsory Registration) Order, 2021: 8., p. 12, dated 2021-03-18 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/11/Electronics-and-Information-Technology-Goods-Requirement-of-Compulsory-Registration-Order-2021-1.pdf#page=12

question: When a former license holder reapplies within one year of expiry for the same product with no changes to standard test requirements, what specific testing actions must be taken, and how should the issuance of the license be handled relative to the final test results? answer:
All possible tests that can be done in a day must be carried out through factory testing, and a sample must be drawn for independent testing [1]. The grant of the license should not be withheld for the receipt of the test report, and an appropriate decision shall be taken after the test report is received in line with the guidelines [1]. question: Who serves as the ex officio Vice-President of the Bureau of Indian Standards under the 2018 Rules?
answer:
The Minister of State or a Deputy Minister, if any, in the Ministry or Department of the Central Government having administrative control of the Bureau serves as the ex officio Vice-President, and where there is no such Minister of State or Deputy Minister, such person as may be nominated by the Central Government shall be the Vice-President [1].

question: I am a manufacturer based overseas looking to bring my non-electronic goods into the Indian market. I heard that BIS certification might be mandatory for imports, but I am unsure if it applies to my specific situation. Can you explain the Foreign Manufacturer Certification Scheme (FMCS) and clarify when a BIS Licence is actually required for importing products?
answer:
The Foreign Manufacturers Certification Scheme (FMCS) is a certification program that allows a foreign manufacturer to obtain a BIS licence to use the Standard Mark on products that conform to an Indian Standard [1]. This scheme applies to all products except for Electronics and Information Technology goods notified by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), which fall under the Registration Scheme [2][1].

A BIS licence is generally voluntary, but it becomes mandatory for products notified by the Government of India under Quality Control Orders (QCOs) [2]. If a product is subject to mandatory compliance with Indian Standards domestically, imported versions of that product must also compulsorily comply with those standards [3]. For such products, the foreign manufacturer is required to obtain a licence from BIS under the FMCS [3].

Key points regarding the FMCS:
*   **Application:** The application must be made by the foreign manufacturer only; an importer cannot apply on their behalf [2].
*   **Authorized Indian Representative (AIR):** The foreign applicant must nominate an Indian resident as an AIR, who will be responsible for compliance with the BIS Act, rules, regulations, and licence terms [2].
*   **Scope:** The licence is granted for a specific product at a manufacturing premise [2].
*   **Validity:** A licence under this scheme may be granted initially for up to two years [2].

To determine if your specific product requires a licence, you can check the list of products under compulsory certification on the official BIS website at https://www.bis.gov.in/index.php/product-certification/productsunder-compulsory-certification/ [2]. You can also search for the relevant Indian Standard for your product at https://www.manakonline.in/MANAK/ApplicationLicenceRelatedrpt [4].

**Sources:**
[1] FMCS (Foreign Manufacturers) Overview: FMCS Overview | https://www.bis.gov.in/fmcs/fmcs-overview/?lang=en
[2] FMCS FAQs: Frequently Asked Questions | https://www.bis.gov.in/fmcs/fmcs-faqs/?lang=en
[3] Guidance Document on Quality Control Orders: 6. Applicability on Imported Goods, p. 2 | https://www.bis.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/Guidance-document-on-QCOs-Revised-1.pdf#page=2
[4] Product Certification FAQ: Frequently Asked Questions | https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/product-certification-faq/?lang=en
